Wynn Resorts Q3 2026 Revenue Falls on Vegas Hold, Boston Strike

Published November 13, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Wynn Resorts reported a third-quarter revenue decline across every one of its properties, with operating revenue falling $144.7 million year over year to roughly $1.69 billion. Net income attributable to the company dropped to $17.3 million, down from $88.3 million in the same quarter last year, with diluted earnings per share falling to $0.17 from $0.85.

Where the decline came from

The drop was spread across Wynn's whole portfolio rather than concentrated in one market. Wynn Palace in Macau led the decline at $51.7 million, followed by Las Vegas operations down $45.8 million, Wynn Macau down $30.1 million, and Encore Boston Harbor down $17.1 million. Adjusted property EBITDAR fell $105.9 million to $464.2 million, with Las Vegas accounting for $44.6 million of that drop, Wynn Palace $34.5 million, Wynn Macau $18.5 million, and Encore Boston Harbor $8.3 million. Adjusted net income came in at $33.9 million, or $0.33 per diluted share, down from $88.7 million, or $0.86 per share, a year earlier.

Vegas hold and a Boston strike

CEO Craig Billings pointed to two specific, largely non-operational factors behind the quarter's softness. "Wynn Las Vegas was also negatively impacted by a hold rate outside of our expected range," Billings said in a statement — a reference to the normal swings in how much of total betting volume a casino keeps on any given quarter's table-games and VIP play, which can move reported revenue without reflecting a change in the underlying business. In Boston, Billings credited the Encore Boston Harbor team with "an excellent job managing through the strike that began in early September, ensuring that we could continue delighting guests at our resort," pointing to a labor disruption as context for that property's decline.

Billings also said Wynn's Al Marjan Island project in the United Arab Emirates remains on track, with interior fit-out underway across all guest rooms as the company works toward a planned September 2027 opening.

What it means for the broader Las Vegas picture

Wynn's results add to a run of soft third-quarter numbers from Las Vegas Strip operators this earnings season, with hold-rate variance and destination softness showing up across multiple companies' reports. For bettors and casino customers, a quarter like this doesn't change odds or game rules at any property — hold-rate swings are a function of how high-stakes play happened to land that quarter, not a change to the house edge on any individual game.
